lessons.title: Land use and problems of towns

objectives: Describe the land-use zones of a town
Describe urban problems and possible solutions
reviewNotes: Teacher to verify the land-use zone model taught (concentric zones) and its fit with Cameroonian towns; the town examples are general.

blocks.md: A town is not made of one kind of land use. The **Central Business District (CBD)** is the busy centre with offices, banks, shops and markets, where land is very expensive and buildings are tall. Around it are older **inner zone** houses, often crowded, then **suburbs** with newer homes and more space, and at the edge the **rural–urban fringe** where farms meet houses. **Industries** are often located along main roads, railways or ports.

blocks.caption: Zones of a town
blocks.alt: Concentric rings from the CBD at the centre to suburbs and the rural-urban fringe.

blocks.title: Why towns grow
blocks.md: Towns grow through **natural increase** and, above all, through **migration** from villages. They also grow when the town offers work in administration, ports, trade and industry, or when a main road or railway brings new activity. Douala (port and industry) and Yaoundé (capital) have grown very fast; Bamenda, Bafoussam and Garoua also attract many people.

blocks.title: Urban problems
blocks.md:
- **Housing shortage** and unplanned neighbourhoods.
- **Traffic jams** and accidents.
- Pressure on **water, electricity and sanitation**; floods where drains are blocked.
- **Unemployment** and street trading in crowded spaces.
- **Pollution** and waste.

**Solutions** include town planning (marking land for homes, roads and parks), building affordable housing, widening and repairing roads and drains, improving public transport, waste collection and recycling, creating jobs and services in rural areas to slow migration, and involving the community through councils. **Urban life** offers jobs, schools and hospitals but brings noise, crowding and a high cost of living; **rural life** is quieter but has fewer services.

blocks.title: Be careful
blocks.md:
- The CBD is not the same as the whole town: it is only the central business area.
- Land use depends on cost, accessibility and history, not on one rule.
- Avoid one-sided answers: always say both advantages and disadvantages of urban life.

blocks.title: Example 1: land use
blocks.statement: Why are tall office buildings found in the CBD and not on the edge of town?
steps: Land in the centre is very expensive and the most accessible.
Building upwards uses limited space well.
So firms pay for the centre and build tall.
blocks.answer: Because land is costly and accessible in the centre, so buildings go up.

blocks.title: Example 2: solution
blocks.statement: Floods occur in a neighbourhood after every heavy storm because drains are blocked. Suggest two solutions.
steps: Clean and repair the drains regularly.
Stop dumping waste in channels and build new drains with the council.
These steps let water flow away.
blocks.answer: Clear and repair drains; stop dumping waste (community action).
